title: Core RSA exponent identity
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $c \in \bbn$ be arbitrary. Then for every $x \in \bbz/p\bbz$,
\[
x^{\,1 + c(p-1)} = x .
\]
This is the form of Fermat's little theorem underlying RSA, and it holds for all $x$, including $x = 0$.
replaced:
Let $p$ be prime. For every $c \in \bbn$ and every $x \in \bbz/p\bbz$,
\[
x^{\,1 + c(p-1)} = x .
\]
This is the form of Fermat's little theorem needed for RSA, valid also at $x = 0$.
